summary: Independently reviewed both editions against all six paragraphs of the selected Greek, including their notes and decision metadata. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the no-repentance assertion, the distinct death and corruption outcomes, the second group’s hope of repentance and renewal, eternal destruction, and the shepherd’s treatment of the sheep. Both visibly distinguish the bracketed editorial restoration from unbracketed text and follow current servant and contextual-repentance policy. The witness disclosures are compatible with the supplied bounded project report and do not require replacing the selected working readings. Acceptance concerns fidelity to the supplied source and disclosure record; it does not authenticate unseen editions, manuscript handwriting, or exhaustive collation.
